the values are those of the reference machine as far as they matter: a vector's segment word is the BIOS segment F000 (DOSBox points the vectors the game does not hook into its F000 callback area; DOS's own handlers would be 0070, a hooked vector a program segment above 0100). Every rule here only needs |segment| > 100 or its remainder by 4; the offsets are not established.
the offset is taken as FF53, the BIOS's default IRET handler that DOSBox points the unused vectors at; the segment is the BIOS's.
slotn is uninitialised in the original when the placement failed before the strip search; 0 is used here and CutFromStrip then cuts strip 0 (the original cuts whatever the stack held).
the original allocates the segment once and gen_clear leaves a few fields alone (the stairs' link and side words, the area beyond 0xBA1D); they start at 0 here and keep their values between calls.

what the real game's stack holds there depends on everything that ran before; the oracle's stack (file reads are stubbed) shows 0 for the first pile and 0x29CB afterwards, and a value above 9 means "no new kind picked, the last one repeats".

the menu bar's sub-menu building (root 0000:0984 and the battle's lists) writes these bytes too (a sub-menu item's text); the rewrite starts it at 0 and keeps only what order_mode_leave writes. The branches below agree for any value other than 0x80, 0x100, one with bit 1 set or one with all of 0x1BE (the value seen in the battle states, 0x1A6D, takes the same branches as 0).

some sets (battlefield 0x38's floor decorations: record 23 of a 5680-byte .ffc, second frame 0x1B40) give a second frame past the end of the decoded file; the original points into whatever follows the block. No second frame here.
glyph clipping at the window's right edge is not reproduced (long lines are cut by the screen edge only).
which keys the original's menu_bar_run takes inside the sheet is not traced; only the Alt keys are passed.
the selection bytes are taken to be 0 outside a battle (the panel is drawn unlit everywhere else, PartyPanel.Draw).

the horizontal centring uses (320 - text width - w->w) / 2 relative to the window; the window offset w->w of card_window is taken as 60 (the card window starts right of the party panel), so the box is centred on the 260 pixels right of the panel. The offset was not checked at run time (it could be 0 when a box comes up over a full screen such as the start screen).
